newsitem.title: UK: Notts Forest shareholders reject takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: Notts Forest shareholders reject takeover bid.

text.p: The future of struggling English Premier League soccer club Nottingham Forest remained unresolved on Tuesday after shareholders rejected a takeover bid by a consortium of local businessmen.

Shareholders at an EGM on Monday night voted 111-79 in favour of the 13 million stg offer from a consortium led by Scottish businessman Sandy Anderson. However, the backing fell short of the 75 percent majority needed for the bid to go ahead.
Forest, facing heavy debts and a battle against relegation, are in urgent need of a cash injection to sign new players to strenghten their squad.
Rival bidders are now expected to emerge and the ownership issue is likely to be settled at another EGM in a few weeks.
One consortium includes Nigel Wray, chairman of property group Burford and owner of Saracens rugby union club.
A spokesman for Wray said on Monday the consortium was planning to make an offer worth around 15 million stg, with the possibility of a flotation to follow.
A group of North American media industry investors is reported to be monitoring the situation while video tycoon Grant Bovey is also expected to rejoin the battle.
